upper_bound.quote: and use at most \(q-1\) cuts in total (standard; details omitted).
upper_bound.witness: Missing statement: for disjoint nonempty A,B with s_A ≥ s_B, the overlay of the A-intervals and B-intervals along the common refinement of [0,s_B], together with bisecting the q−|A|−|B| remaining intervals, requires at most (|A|−1)+|B|+(q−|A|−|B|) = q−1 new distinct interior marks, and every cell in [0,s_B] appears once in each row so the pieces pair up with only the A-tail of length Γ unpaired. The text names the construction but explicitly omits the count of cuts and the pairing verification, which is the quantitative core of why Xiang's n marks suffice when q=n+1.
upper_bound.load_bearing: Section 3 obtains Liu ≤ 2^n/(2^{n+1}−1) solely by invoking the upper half of the refinement lemma (D ≤ Γ with ≤ q−1 cuts); without the omitted cut-count argument the bound is unproved.

parsed.notes: Drafting lemma (greedy optimal, Liu gets (1+D)/2) is correct. Lower bound via binary lengths and the tree-component subset-sum argument is complete and correct. Upper bound construction (overlay with ≤ q−1 cuts) is only sketched with 'details omitted'; the omitted count appears correct but is not written.
